facts.content: Patient presents with diarrhea for 3 days.
Patient has 4-5 bowel movements per day, with varying consistency from watery to loose.
Patient experiences mild abdominal pain.
Patient experienced one episode of vomiting.
Patient denies blood or mucus in stool.
Patient reports possible low-grade fever and decreased appetite.
Patient reports drinking well, with no recent travel, no suspicious foods consumed, and no medications tried.
facts.source_text: drinking well; no recent travel; no suspicious foods; no meds tried

facts.content: Patient has a history of asthma.
Patient is taking Lexapro.
Patient has no known drug allergies.
Patient's father had hypertension.
Patient's father died of bowel cancer at age 62, around 10 years ago.
facts.source_text: father died of bowel CA at 62 (~10 y ago)

facts.content: Acute diarrhea for 3 days with mild abdominal pain and one episode of vomiting, no blood or mucus, maintaining oral intake.
facts.source_text: Acute diarrhea x3 d with mild abdo pain, 1x emesis; no blood/mucus; maintaining PO intake

facts.content: History of asthma.
Family history of colon cancer and hypertension in father.
Encourage fluid intake and use oral rehydration solution such as Dioralyte.
Advise a soft, easily digested diet, starting with crackers, toast, and jam, then boiled vegetables and mashed foods.
facts.source_text: Diet: “soft”/easily digested—crackers, toast, jam; then boiled veg/mash

facts.content: Advise to avoid milk, dairy (except yoghurt), meat, fish, and eggs during acute phase.
facts.source_text: Avoid during acute: milk/dairy (except yoghurt), meat, fish, eggs

facts.content: Yoghurt is allowed, as it is a probiotic.
Reintroduce meat, eggs, and fish only after 48 hours without diarrhea.
facts.source_text: Reintroduce meat/eggs/fish only after 48 h without diarrhea

facts.content: Advise to seek re-evaluation if symptoms persist for more than one week, if blood appears in the stool, if bowel movement frequency increases to six to eight times per day, or if signs of dehydration appear.
facts.source_text: Red flags/return: stool sample if persists >1 wk or if blood in stool; seek care if frequency ≥6–8/day or signs of dehydration

facts.content: Follow-up as needed or for worsening symptoms.
